page.overview:
Who is Shub-Niggurath?

Shub-Niggurath, also known as The Black Goat of the Woods with a Thousand Young, is an Outer God in the Cthulhu Mythos. The character was first mentioned in H. P. Lovecraft's revision story "The Last Test" (1928); in Lovecraft's fiction, she is never actually described, but is frequently mentioned or called upon in incantations. Shub-Niggurath is also referenced in the works of other Mythos authors, including Robert Bloch, August Derleth, Ramsey Campbell, Lin Carter, and Brian Lumley.

Shub-Niggurath is an Outer God (or Outer Goddess) in the pantheon. She is a perverse fertility deity, said to appear as an "hellish cloud-like entity". (: "Selected Letters 5.875")

She has been described as an enormous mass which extrudes black tentacles, slime-dripping mouths, and short, writhing goat legs (: S. Petersen's Field Guide to Cthulhu Monsters). Small creatures are continually spat forth by the monstrosity, which are either consumed into the miasmatic form or escape to some monstrous life elsewhere. (source?)

Shub-Niggurath is the wife of the Not-to-Be-Named One (: The Mound) and of Yog-Sothoth which birthed the twins Nug and Yeb. (: Selected Letters 4.617, 5.875)

Also known as: Black Goat of the Woods.

connections.short_description: Glynda (second name undisclosed) is a fictional character created by Josh Finney for his Casefile: Arkham Mythos stories. She made her first appearance in the 2016 graphic novel Casefile: Arkham- Nightmare on the Canvas.
